correctness.rationale: The four switched vertices form an independent set; every incidence column into that set has zero or two ones, and J4/2−I4 complements the two-one columns and fixes the zero columns. Conjugation by the displayed involution proves adjacency cospectrality. Both graphs are cubic and connected. The unique triangle has external neighbors 4,5,6 whose common-neighbor intersection is {0} in G and empty in H; this proves nonisomorphism independent of the dynamics. A fresh exact enumeration of all 16,384 states per graph, with vertex v at bit v and at least two of its three open neighbors needed for output 1, reproduces every displayed count, both statewise digests and the witness trajectories. Fixed-point counts are 18/14, recurrent period-two state counts are 402/150 (hence 201/75 orbits), and the total p=1 basins are 3504/4036. There are 12 depth-nine states on G and 60 depth-seven states on H, and no states at greater depth. The witness cycles begin, respectively, with 8194↔384 at time nine and 912↔8205 at time seven. The exact characteristic polynomial also matches. The literature supports minimum order fourteen for connected nonisomorphic cospectral cubic graphs. The sentence saying Godsil–McKay prove the minimum is imprecise: their §2.3(c) reports it and cites the earlier census. This does not affect the minimum or any proof in the record.
residual_risks: The enumeration uses exact finite software, not a formal proof certificate; the maximum is first recurrence entry, not maximum time to unanimity.

evidence: Godsil–McKay's local switching theorem gives cospectrality and the paper reports cubic order fourteen as the minimum; the construction is used, not claimed as new.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These theorems supply the graph relation or the range of allowed periods, not the counts and sharp times. In particular, a universal period bound cannot decide how many initial states arrive at each periodic component or at each depth.

checked_sources: Independently regenerated exact period–depth census; minimum-order graph census; earlier separate degree-six comparisons
value.rationale: The first available order for a cubic adjacency-cospectral pair fixes a natural comparison class before enumeration. This exact benchmark separates three useful notions—fixed-state abundance, collective fixed basin and worst entry time—and shows that the graph with more fixed states can have a smaller basin. The full period–depth distributions can test proposed spectral predictions for strict-majority dynamics without relying on a tie convention or a sample of starting states.
residual_risks: Only two of the graphs at this order are evaluated; there is no sharp bound for the entire order-fourteen class and no general asymptotic conclusion.
